# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to get this manual information to Blind, but I can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures anyway. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. So I must relay through Deaf: I gesture the manual info to Deaf, then Deaf must speak it to Blind (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

I need a gesture encoding for the three light→wire pairs: blue→yellow, green→green, red→blue. Let me use distinct symbols for colors, pairing each light with its cut color in sequence, using a separator gesture.

Let me define a simple mapping: 👆=blue, 🖐=green, ✊=red (lights), and 👇=yellow, 🤞=green, ☝=blue (cut colors), 👏=separator/pair-break.

I'll gesture: light-blue, cut-yellow, PAIR, light-green, cut-green, PAIR, light-red, cut-blue.

This is turn 1, and speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so I go first, but only Deaf can see me. Deaf goes last this round, so Deaf receives my gesture this same round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👇", "👏", "🖐", "🤞", "👏", "✊", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. No other markings reach my hands. What does the manual say?
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows zero. Light is blue. Button is large and says push to defuse. Three wires: one blue, two green, three yellow.

I now know the light is blue, so per the manual: blue → cut yellow. The button says "push to defuse" — but the manual says printed bait should NOT be trusted, so pushing the button is the fuse/trap. I must NOT push it. I need to tell Blind to cut the yellow wire (wire position 3, since Deaf said "three yellow"), and definitely not push the button.

But wait — Blind cannot see colors or printed text, only feel. Blind said wires are just at positions 1,2,3 with no markings reaching their hands — meaning Blind can't tell which wire is which color by touch. So I need Deaf to relay the color→position mapping, or I relay the wire color to cut via gesture to Deaf, who then speaks it to Blind.

My gesture to Deaf established: blue→yellow, green→green, red→blue. Deaf now knows light is blue, so cut yellow. Deaf can figure this out from my gesture and speak "cut yellow" to Blind. Deaf already has all info needed. I should confirm/reinforce and also gesture NOT to push button.

Let me gesture a clear "danger/no" symbol for the button, and confirm blue→yellow again to make sure Deaf got it right, since this is critical.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "👏", "👆", "👇"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting to hear the manual. My hands find: button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, nothing else. Please relay manual instructions and anything Deaf gestures about wire colors.

Blind is waiting on Deaf to speak the info, but Deaf hasn't spoken yet (Deaf goes last in turn order, after me). Deaf received my gestures in turns 1 and 2 but hasn't relayed to Blind via speech yet — Deaf's messages so far were only to me/everyone about the display. I need to wait for Deaf to speak to Blind. Since I can't speak, I can't directly tell Blind anything myself — I can only gesture to Deaf.

I already gestured the mapping twice. Deaf should now speak "cut yellow, don't push button" to Blind. Let me reinforce once more clearly, in case my gestures weren't parsed, and also make sure Deaf understands they must relay to Blind by voice since I cannot.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "☝", "👏", "🖐", "🤞", "👏", "👆", "👇", "👏", "👎", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows zero, light is blue, three wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Button says push to defuse. What does the manual say to do given this state? I will wait for your instruction before touching anything.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot read your gestures without a code yet. Let's use this: point number of fingers up for which wire to cut, thumbs up if button should be pushed, thumbs down if not. Gesture that now please.

Deaf has now spoken to Blind, relaying the wire colors and positions correctly: wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Light is blue → manual says cut yellow → that's wire 3. Button should NOT be pushed (it's bait/fuse).

Deaf proposes a code: number of fingers = wire number to cut, thumbs up/down for button. I'll use that now since it's clear and unambiguous. I'll show 3 fingers (✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3-ish... let me use unambiguous finger-count gestures) — I'll use ☝ (one), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three) as finger counts, and 👎 for thumbs down (don't push).

Wire 3 = yellow = correct cut. So: 3 fingers up, thumbs down on button.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see rock-on hand shape and thumbs down. I read that as wire 3, yellow, and do not push the button. Gesture thumbs up to confirm this is correct, or thumbs down if I misread.

Deaf correctly interpreted my gesture: wire 3 (yellow), don't push button. This matches the manual: light is blue → cut yellow → that's wire 3. I need to confirm this is correct with thumbs up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Deaf has confirmed the correct interpretation (wire 3, yellow, don't push button), and should now relay this to Blind by speech. Nothing new for me to do right now — I'll wait to see if Blind needs anything further or if the round completes.

```
wait()
```
